_evidence: Entry block behind pointer global 0x006097b0 (0x0042458b sets it to 0x006099c0 + index*0x5d8; 0x00422397 caps its int32 record count at +0x18 below 0x48, and 0x38 + 0x48*0x14 = 0x5d8 is the block size). 0x00424625 reads the header x/y/z at [ebx]/[ebx+4]/[ebx+8] (0x0042469c.., 0x0042471a..), walks 0x14-byte records from +0x38 reading x/y/z at [edi]/[edi+4]/[edi+8] and the kind at [edi+0xc] (cmp 1 at 0x00424672, cmp 2 at 0x00424682, anything else takes 0x00424718), and stops when the incremented index equals [ebx+0x18] (0x0042477a); it writes only +0x20..+0x37. A count of 0 (or above the records present) runs past the block until ecx wraps, so the count is 1..8 and all 8 records are described; kinds 0..3 give 1, 2 and two 'other' values. Coordinates are unconstrained i32: the code only subtracts/adds and compares signed (wrapping is not a fault), so every value is valid for the original and both directions of each jge/jle are reached.
